root_idea.summary: The lexical center is كُوبٌ, a handleless cup or drinking vessel, with أَكْوَابٌ as its plural.
root_idea.development: The packet supplies no abstract root principle beyond this concrete vessel term. Alongside the vessel noun and its Quranic plural, it records distinct derived and separately vocalized Classical Arabic branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested broken plural is displayed under its normalized singular dictionary citation form كُوبٌ.

senses.definition: A handleless drinking cup or vessel.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the broken plural أَكْوَابٌ. The source descriptions of the Quranic vessel include one with neither handle nor spout.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the construction describes drinking with a كُوبٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pound or bray something using a small stone, such as a فِهْر or كُوبَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II verb; the implementing stone is described as one that fills the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slenderness of the neck together with largeness of the head.
A sigh, grief, or regret over something that has passed or escaped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical item; its formation is tentatively related to كَأْبَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game, identified in different reports as nard or chess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identification varies by report; the names نَرْد and شِطْرَنْج are recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small drum slender in the middle; in one report, the name is applied to the barbat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The barbat identification is attributed to some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small stone that fills the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Given as equivalent to a فِهْر.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I drinking construction is represented.
The Form II pounding construction is represented.
Pointer-only reference to the Form I entry.
The handleless cup or vessel and its plural are represented under the Quranic form.
The grief or regret meaning is represented.
The game and musical-instrument branches are represented separately.

cautions: The QAC group attests only the plural أَكْوَابٌ; the public form is normalized to the singular citation noun كُوبٌ.
The consonantal root record contains differently vocalized nouns with distinct meanings; these branches are kept separate from the Quranic vessel noun.
